Observed temperatures throughout the day have hovered near 26–28°C, with current evening readings around 26–27°C confirming the peak. This positioning aligns with typical September conditions in Metro Manila, where the southwest monsoon often caps maxima below seasonal averages. The outcome could shift only if sustained clear breaks unexpectedly develop before midnight or if official station data revises the daily maximum upward due to localized microclimate effects.

**Official National Weather Service forecasts for Miami on September 7, 2026, call for a daytime high near 89–90°F under partly to mostly sunny skies early, followed by showers and thunderstorms likely after midday.** This pattern—typical for South Florida in early September—features high humidity, light southwest winds shifting southeast, and afternoon convection that increases cloud cover and rainfall chances (60–70%), which tends to cap peak temperatures by reducing solar heating.

Recent observations reinforce this outlook. The prior day (September 6) reached 92°F before storms developed, while September climatology at Miami International Airport shows average daily highs of 89–90°F with frequent afternoon convection. Multiple model runs and local forecasts align on maximums in the upper 80s to low 90s, with heat indices exceeding 100°F but actual air temperatures moderated by moisture and cloud build-up.

Trader positioning reflects this consensus: the 90–91°F bin leads at 64% implied probability because it matches the most probable official high under standard convective conditions, while 92–93°F (26%) captures upside risk if storms are delayed or weaker. Lower bins (88–89°F at 14.5%) account for stronger or earlier rain suppression. No unusual atmospheric setup, such as suppressed convection or anomalous ridging, has emerged to shift the distribution significantly. Updated NWS briefings or real-time observations through the afternoon will provide the clearest signals for any late adjustments.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Latest official forecasts from the Chongqing Meteorological Observatory and supporting global models point to a peak of 37–38°C on September 8 under mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies with minimal precipitation.** Persistent high pressure and weak southerly flow are maintaining the “autumn tiger” heatwave that produced observed highs of 37–39°C in recent days, with the urban heat-island effect in the Sichuan Basin amplifying afternoon readings.  

Model consensus clusters tightly around these values, with only modest spread that could allow a brief spike to 39°C or a cap near 36–37°C if afternoon cloud build-up occurs. Historical early-September normals sit near 28–29°C, underscoring the current anomaly. The market’s heavy weighting toward 38°C (45.5%) and 37°C (33.5%) therefore reflects the narrow but well-supported forecast envelope, while lower-probability outcomes for 39°C or below 37°C capture residual model uncertainty ahead of the final observational window.

Updated Météo-France and NOAA model runs expected in the next 24–48 hours will further refine resolution odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Ben Gurion International Airport in degrees Celsius on 9 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=LLBG

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from agencies and models indicate Tokyo's maximum temperature on September 9 will likely fall in the 30–32°C range, aligning with market-implied odds clustered around those outcomes. Southerly flows, high humidity near 80%, and afternoon thunderstorm potential from regional instability are key variables, as cloud cover and precipitation timing can suppress peak readings by 1–2°C or allow brief clears to push higher. Historical September baselines average near 28–29°C, but current patterns reflect above-normal warmth moderated by frequent showers. Updated model runs and official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance over the next 48 hours will refine these thresholds ahead of market resolution.

This positioning reflects the balance between residual cool anomalies from the prior days and the emerging high-pressure ridge supporting gradual recovery, with model spread remaining narrow enough to favor outcomes clustered tightly around 20–21°C over higher or lower thresholds.

title: Highest temperature in Istanbul on September 9?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Istanbul Airport in degrees Celsius on 9 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=LTFM

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
